campbell.title: Campbell City Council — November 2, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council meeting on November 2, 2026, centered on a proposal to replace the Campbell Technology Park office campus with 290 homes. The Council approved the proposal in a 3-1 vote. It also approved a one-year contract for police recruitment marketing and heard neighborhood residents voice concerns about housing development in single-family areas.
keyTopics: Campbell Technology Park housing project: The Council approved plans to demolish the roughly 17-acre office/R&D campus and build 290 homes (27 detached houses and 263 townhome-style condos, 20% of them affordable to lower-income households). The proposal passed 3-1, with Mayor Furtado voting no. Staff said state "builder's remedy" law sharply limits the city's ability to deny or reduce the project.

Traffic, trees and neighbor concerns: Staff said the project would add about 1,368 net daily trips and require new crosswalks near Campbell Technology Parkway and McGlincy Lane. Discussion also covered a separate city restriping project at Camden and White Oaks. Residents of the neighboring Paseo de Palomas senior mobile home park supported the lower-density plan but asked that their private entrance remain restricted to emergency access and that the redwood trees along their fence be kept. 116 trees are slated for removal.

Police recruitment contract: The Council approved a one-year agreement with All Star Talent, funded with $175,000 from the budget, to run online police recruiting and marketing. Police staff said applications rose from about 57 in 2022 to 355 last year; one councilmember said she supported it but wanted the program's effectiveness reviewed more closely.

Residents on neighborhood housing: Several White Oaks Manor residents said they support housing in the right places but oppose projects that replace single-family homes with townhomes. They asked for clearer, objective rules. One speaker asked what happens once the city meets its state housing targets.

Announcements covered Election Day on Nov. 3, openings on city boards and commissions, and a Veterans Day ceremony scheduled for Nov. 11 at 9 a.m. on the Orchard City Green. Poll hours were 7 a.m. to 8 p.m., and mailed ballots needed a Nov. 3 postmark.

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — November 18, 2026
saratoga.summary: The agenda for the Saratoga City Council's November 18, 2026, meeting listed a public hearing on an appeal of a denied 69-unit housing project on Quito Road, along with four general business items covering a possible Mountain Winery annexation, the Civic Theater's management, a historic-property tax agreement, and Saratoga Village's economy. It also included a ceremonial recognition of the Scareatoga Scarecrows organizers and routine consent items such as past minutes and bill payments.
keyTopics: The agenda listed an appeal of the Planning Commission's denial of a 69-unit project at 14076 Quito Road (55 townhome/condominium units plus 14 attached affordable accessory dwelling units on a 3.85-acre site split into 14 lots). Staff recommended upholding the appeal and conditionally approving the project.
Mountain Winery annexation discussion: Council was asked to direct staff on any further work it wanted done on a potential annexation of the property.
Saratoga Civic Theater: a proposal to authorize the City Manager's Office to move management and operations of the theater to South Bay Musical Theatre.
Mills Act agreement for 19490 Glen Una Drive: a resolution that would authorize the City Manager to enter into a historic property preservation agreement for the landmark-designated property.

The agenda included a Saratoga Village economic vitality update with ideas from community engagement and an invitation for the Council to give staff additional direction. It also listed ceremonial recognition of the Scareatoga Scarecrows organizers (Laurel Perusa, Lynda Pevar, Tina Liddie, Cody Teerlink).

los-altos.title: Los Altos City Council — October 27, 2026
los-altos.summary: The agenda for the Los Altos City Council's October 27, 2026, meeting listed routine business such as approving past minutes, reviewing city investments, and buying maintenance vehicles. It also listed contracts for a park expansion and a police backup generator, a proposed pay change for the City Manager, and an extension of a temporary moratorium on certain detention-related facilities.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a contract with Lignum Mellis of San Francisco to complete the Building B Park Expansion Project, not to exceed $166,225, plus up to 10% for construction contingency.
The agenda listed a $417,400 contract with ELECCO of Milpitas to replace the Police Department's backup generator, with a construction contingency of up to 15%.
The agenda listed an amendment to the City Manager's employment agreement setting a base salary of $375,000 effective July 5, 2026, and a yearly cost-of-living-style adjustment beginning July 2027.

The agenda listed an interim urgency ordinance extending Ordinance No. 2026-548, a temporary moratorium on filing, accepting, or processing applications for detention or custodial facilities and custodial processing facilities.

The agenda listed a Cal Water presentation on water conservation measures and a resolution approving a Transit Signal Priority Policy on behalf of the Santa Clara Valley Transportation Authority (VTA).

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — November 17, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The agenda for the November 17, 2026, Los Gatos Town Council meeting listed routine business such as approving past meeting minutes and payment records, along with a few items on zoning rules, completed street projects, and staffing. One item would add a full-time Senior Planner position to the town's 2026-27 budget.
keyTopics: The agenda listed approval of minutes from the October 28, 2026, closed session and the November 2, 2026, special Town Council meeting.
The agenda listed adoption of an ordinance amending Chapter 29 (Zoning Regulations) of the Town Code.

The agenda listed authorization of a Certificate of Acceptance and Notice of Completion for the 2026 Annual Curb, Gutter, and Sidewalk Maintenance Project, with the Town Manager authorized to sign related completion paperwork.
The agenda listed approval and ratification of the accounts payable check registers and payroll report.
The agenda listed consideration of adding a full-time Senior Planner position to the Fiscal Year 2026-27 budget.

san-jose.body: Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole
san-jose.title: San José Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole — November 18, 2026
san-jose.summary: The agenda listed the San José Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole, which sets the City Council's agendas, for November 18, 2026. It listed a review of the draft agenda for the December 1, 2026, Council meeting, with the November 24, 2026, final agenda review marked cancelled, along with several Council-sponsored community events and a proposal to create a new cultural district.
keyTopics: The agenda listed the November 24, 2026, Final Agenda review as cancelled.
The agenda listed a review of the December 1, 2026, Draft Agenda, including adding new items, assigning "time certain" slots, and checking notice waiver requirements.
Proposed establishment of the La Avenida Cultural District, brought by Mayor Mahan and Councilmembers Ortiz, Campos, Tordillos, and Candelas.

Council-sponsored special events to spend City funds and accept donated materials and services: a Senior Symposium (District 9, retroactive), a bus visit to the Vietnam Traveling Memorial Wall (District 7, retroactive), and various events (District 6, retroactive and new).
A proclamation and Council-sponsored Holiday Children Book Drive (District 1), plus a request for Mayor's travel approval.

mountain-view.title: Mountain View Tennis Advisory Committee — November 19, 2026
mountain-view.summary: The agenda for the November 19, 2026, Mountain View Tennis Advisory Committee meeting listed routine business: approving past meeting minutes, planning the committee's 2027 meeting schedule and work plan, and choosing a committee chair while recruiting new members. Residents were also given a slot to speak on topics not on the agenda.
keyTopics: The agenda listed approval of minutes from a previous meeting.
The agenda listed the committee's 2027 meeting schedule and work plan for consideration.
The agenda listed nomination of a Tennis Advisory Committee Chair and recruitment of new members.
The agenda included an Oral Communications period where residents may speak for up to three minutes on topics not on the agenda.

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — November 17, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: The agenda for the November 17, 2026, Sunnyvale City Council meeting listed a construction contract for Plaza del Sol, a proposed local emergency declaration tied to a developing El Niño event, and several items on housing and RV/vehicle parking. It also listed a contract amendment and salary range change for the City Attorney.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a $3,268,600 contract with S & H Construction, Inc. for the Plaza del Sol Phase II ReBid Project, with a 10% contingency of $326,860 and a $1,067,998 budget modification.
The agenda listed a resolution proclaiming a local emergency in Sunnyvale due to the developing 2026-2027 El Niño event.
The agenda listed adoption of Ordinance No. 3263-26, which would change the rules on paying an in-lieu fee to satisfy the city's below-market-rate ownership housing requirement.

The agenda listed items on homelessness and vehicle housing: directing staff to plan and begin environmental review of an interim housing community at 1240 Fair Oaks Way, considering an RV permit parking program on Caribbean Drive, and studying a safe parking pilot at 241 Commercial Street ($122,000 budget modification).
The agenda listed an amendment to City Attorney Rebecca Moon's employment agreement and a resolution increasing the City Attorney's salary range.

cupertino.title: Cupertino City Council — November 17, 2026
cupertino.summary: The agenda for the November 17, 2026, Cupertino City Council meeting listed a closed-door session on two lawsuits against the city, a recognition of Small Business Saturday, and a consent calendar of routine items. It also listed several policy items, including community funding and festival fee waivers, updates to the Council's procedures manual, and a proposed change to City Council compensation.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a closed-session conference with legal counsel on two existing lawsuits in Santa Clara County Superior Court: Lixin (Leon) Chen, et al. v. City of Cupertino and Yes in My Backyard, et al. v. City of Cupertino.
The agenda listed a recognition of Small Business Saturday, which falls on November 28, 2026.
The consent calendar listed a maximum rate schedule for Recology's recycling, organics, and solid waste collection and processing services (Rate Period Seven).
The consent calendar listed adoption of the 2026 Emergency Operations Plan and an amendment to the Cupertino Library lease covering aquarium maintenance and janitorial services.

The agenda listed Council subcommittee recommendations on the Community Funding Policy and festival fee waivers, along with a proposed ordinance amending Municipal Code Section 2.16.020 on City Council compensation.

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara Stevens Creek Corridor Steering Committee — November 23, 2026
santa-clara.summary: The agenda listed a Stevens Creek Corridor Steering Committee meeting, held by Zoom webinar, for the group that guides a joint study of how to improve transportation along Stevens Creek Boulevard. The study is a partnership among San José, Santa Clara, Cupertino, Santa Clara County, and VTA. The agenda listed one action item (approving past meeting minutes) and several information items on corridor activities, bike and pedestrian projects, and next steps.
keyTopics: The agenda listed approval of the Steering Committee's January 28, 2026, meeting summary as an action item.
The agenda listed an information item on current corridor activities.
The agenda listed an information item on 2016 Measure B Complete Streets bicycle and pedestrian improvements along the Stevens Creek corridor.
The agenda listed an information item on next steps for the corridor study.

The agenda said the public could join by Zoom (registration required) or phone and speak using 'Raise Hand' or *9, with usually two minutes per speaker and double time for speakers using a translator.

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — November 17, 2026
milpitas.summary: The agenda for the November 17, 2026, Milpitas City Council meeting listed a mix of routine housekeeping items and contracts for the city to consider. Items included the 2027 meeting schedule, winter holiday closure arrangements, labor agreements for two employee groups, and several multi-vendor purchasing and services contracts.
keyTopics: Winter recess and 2027 schedule: the agenda listed a holiday closure schedule resolution that would let the City Manager or a designee approve and sign project-related documents and urgent administrative items while the Council is on winter recess, plus approval of the 2027 Council meeting calendar.

Employee contracts: the Council was set to consider successor labor agreements running July 1, 2026, through June 30, 2030, with the Milpitas Professional and Technical Group and the Mid-Management and Confidential Unit, along with a related FY2026-27 budget appropriation.
Homeless outreach: an amendment to the city's contract with WeHope for homeless outreach, assessment, and mobile hygiene services was listed, adding $163,522 to the contract.

Vendor contracts: the agenda listed authorization for agreements with six firms for as-requested temporary staffing (up to $1.5 million total over five years) and with 74 vendors for citywide maintenance supplies, materials, and related services over five years.

Stormwater maintenance agreements: two agreements were listed for stormwater management facilities, one with Extra Shine Car Wash at 554 South Main Street and one with KB Home South Bay at 2001 Tarob Court.

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto City Council — November 16, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The agenda listed a joint study session of the City Council and Utilities Advisory Commission on the reliability of Palo Alto's water supply, along with a set of housing, infrastructure, park, and city-administration items. Housing was a major theme, with items on redevelopment incentives, a rezoning at 470 Olive Avenue, and a request for affordable housing proposals at 340 Portage Avenue.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a joint study session of the Council and Utilities Advisory Commission on water-supply reliability, with presentations from city staff, the Bay Area Water Supply & Conservation Agency (BAWSCA), and the Yosemite Rivers Alliance, plus a public comment slot.

The agenda listed a proposal to rezone 470 Olive Avenue from single-family residential to medium-density mixed use and change its North Ventura Coordinated Area Plan designation to match the zoning of the adjacent parcel at 2951 El Camino Real. The changes would support city staff's determination to add the property to the housing inventory.
The agenda listed a proposal to authorize a request for proposals and a local funding contribution for an affordable housing development at 340 Portage Avenue (Matadero Creek).

The agenda listed implementation of Housing Element Program 3.9(A), which aims to identify incentives at strategic locations to shift the economic benefit of redevelopment from commercial toward home building.
The agenda listed a $1,555,050 local matching-funds agreement with the Santa Clara Valley Water District for the Newell Road/San Francisquito Creek Bridge Replacement Project.
